title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: which clock the final demurrage line is measured on
content:
## Scope

This rule of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category fixes, for the final demurrage line of a per-container record, the clock that is measured, its start and stop dates, its days used and the free days it is measured against, according to the clock model of the product on the record and the direction of the record.

## Rule

1. Under the separate clock model, the demurrage clock of an import record runs from the discharge date to the full gate-out date against the import demurrage free days, and that of an export record from the full gate-in date to the loading date against the export demurrage free days.
2. Under the combined clock model, the merged clock of an import record runs from the discharge date to the empty return date and that of an export record from the empty pickup date to the loading date, against the merged free days of the direction.
3. The days used are the stop date minus the start date in calendar days; in the product's own count this is the calendar days from start to stop, less the product's clock start offset, increased by one, which comes to the same figure where the offset is one day.

## Which dates bound the demurrage clock

| Product clock model | Direction | Clock runs from | Clock runs to | Measured against |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| separate | import | discharge | full gate-out | import demurrage free days |
| separate | export | full gate-in | loading | export demurrage free days |
| combined | import | discharge | empty return | merged import free days |
| combined | export | empty pickup | loading | merged export free days |

## Example (hypothetical dates, offset of one day)

A separate-model export record goes through the gate full on 4 May and is loaded on 13 May: the demurrage clock has used 9 days, 13 May less 4 May. Had the product been a combined-model product with an empty pickup on 28 April, the merged clock would instead run from 28 April to 13 May and would have used 15 days.

## Points of judgement

**Q: On a combined import record, does the demurrage clock stop at full gate-out?**
A: No. The merged clock runs on to the empty return date; which of its days are demurrage days is a separate question.
